knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A claim can be checked only when its referent, test standard and verifier are known. Whether the product smells pleasant (option 0) and whether it is cheaper (option 2) do not test an environmental claim.
The lesson requires the product, reason, evidence and date to be recorded so the choice can be reviewed. Recording nothing (option 0) or only the price (option 2) leaves no evidence trail.
The lesson says a biodegradable claim may refer to a single ingredient, under specific conditions, and not to the whole product.

practicalCriteria: Learner identifies, for a supplied product claim, what the claim refers to, the test or standard behind it and who verified it.
Learner reads the hazard statements, signal word and disposal guidance from a supplied label and SDS and states how they affect the product choice.
Learner records the product, reason, evidence and date on the approved product record, and leaves out any claim without a source.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Approved product record with the evidence for each claim and a review date
stopWorkCriteria: Learner approves a product on the strength of a marketing claim alone
